### Inverse-Distance Weighted KNN Models ($k = 3, 5, 10$)

To evaluate how neighborhood size affects distance-weighted classification, we specify a KNN classifier using the `kknn` engine with `weight_func = "inv"`, which weights each neighbor's vote inversely by its distance ($w_i = 1 / d_i$). We pair this specification with `knn_rec` inside a `tidymodels` workflow and evaluate $k \in \{3, 5, 10\}$ across our 5 cross-validation folds using classification accuracy and multi-class ROC-AUC.

```{r}

fit_inv_knn <- function(k_val) {
  spec <- nearest_neighbor(neighbors = k_val, weight_func = "inv") |>
    set_engine("kknn") |>
    set_mode("classification")

  wf <- workflow() |>
    add_recipe(knn_rec) |>
    add_model(spec)

  fit_resamples(
    wf,
    resamples = spotify_folds,
    metrics = metric_set(accuracy, roc_auc)
  ) |>
    collect_metrics() |>
    mutate(neighbors = k_val, weight_func = "inv")
}

inv_results <- bind_rows(
  fit_inv_knn(3),
  fit_inv_knn(5),
  fit_inv_knn(10)
) |>
  select(neighbors, weight_func, .metric, mean, std_err)

inv_results |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "5-fold CV performance for inverse-distance KNN (k = 3, 5, 10)"
  )
```

Across the candidate neighborhood sizes, 5-fold cross-validation performance improves steadily as $k$ increases from 3 to 10. Specifically, $k = 10$ achieves the highest mean classification accuracy (`0.4551`, SE = `0.0033`) and multi-class ROC-AUC (`0.7654`, SE = `0.0044`), outperforming both $k = 3$ (`0.4032` accuracy, `0.7040` ROC-AUC) and $k = 5$ (`0.4171` accuracy, `0.7325` ROC-AUC). Because inverse-distance weighting downweights more distant points, increasing the neighborhood size to $k = 10$ reduces prediction variance in overlapping regions of the audio feature space while preserving sensitivity to the closest neighbors.
